identity.name: Saar Basin Territory
native_names: Territoire du Bassin de la Sarre
alt_names: Saar under the League of Nations

land.text: the Saar Basin: 'the portions of the Prussian Rhenish Trier Region and the Bavarian district of the Palatinate' set out in Article 48 of the Treaty of Versailles; the territory 'closely corresponds with the modern German state of Saarland, but was slightly smaller in area'

predecessors.note: Rhenish Prussia and the Bavarian Palatinate, German land until the Treaty of Versailles took effect on 10 January 1920. The weimar-republic dossier records the loss.

land.text: 'On 1 March, Germany re-integrated the region into the German Reich'

successors.note: After the 13 January 1935 plebiscite (90.8% for Germany) and the League Council's approval of 17 January 1935; Josef Bürckel became Reichskommissar. The nazi-germany dossier records the gain in March 1935.

correction.text: the Saar Basin: 'the portions of the Prussian Rhenish Trier Region and the Bavarian district of the Palatinate' set out in Article 48 of the Treaty of Versailles; the territory 'closely corresponds with the modern German state of Saarland, but was slightly smaller in area'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for the Saar Basin Territory (its German Empire and Weimar shapes keep the Saar inside Germany). The page gives no area in km2 (page silent) and a population of 812,000 in 1933; it says the territory 'closely corresponds with the modern German state of Saarland, but was slightly smaller in area', so the modern Saarland is the best name. The Article 48 boundary is not reproduced on the page.

region.text: the Saar Basin: 'the portions of the Prussian Rhenish Trier Region and the Bavarian district of the Palatinate' set out in Article 48 of the Treaty of Versailles; the territory 'closely corresponds with the modern German state of Saarland, but was slightly smaller in area'

ledger.note: 10 January 1920: the Saar Basin Territory is created under a League of Nations Governing Commission. The page's infobox 'Treaty of Versailles took effect: 10 January 1920'; 'governed by the five-person Governing Commission'; the page has the UK and France occupying and governing it under a League of Nations mandate for fifteen years; 'Its coalfields were also to be ceded to France'.

region.text: the Saar territory, re-integrated into the German Reich

ledger.note: 1 March 1935: the Saar returns to Germany. 'On 1 March, Germany re-integrated the region into the German Reich', after the plebiscite of 13 January 1935 ('The overwhelming majority, 90.8%, voted to re-join the German Reich') and the League Council's approval on 17 January.

1 March 1935: the Saar Basin Territory ceases. The referendum page: 'The Saar once again became part of Germany on 1 March 1935' after 'a referendum on territorial status ... on 13 January 1935' (477,089 votes or 90.73% for Germany, 46,613 or 8.86% for the status quo, 2,124 or 0.40% for France; turnout 97.86%).

certainty.note: The frontier is the one laid down in Articles 45-50 of the Treaty of Versailles (Article 48 sets out the boundary); it did not move in fifteen years.

sources.title: Territory of the Saar Basin
sources.note: Identity, 10 January 1920 and 1 March 1935, capital, 1933 population 812,000, Versailles Articles 45-50, composition of the territory, plebiscite of 13 January 1935. The page has no km2 figure.

sources.title: 1935 Saar status referendum
sources.note: Result figures, turnout and the 1 March 1935 return to Germany; silent on area and on the 1920 creation.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the Saar as a state. Other dossiers already use the slug saar-basin-territory as counterpart (weimar-republic, nazi-germany). The pages give no km2 figure for the territory, so no infobox comparison was possible; the page's 'slightly smaller than modern Saarland' is the whole of the evidence on extent. The French coal-mine ownership (the 'coalfields were also to be ceded to France') and the customs union with France are not territorial and are not drawn. The Governing Commission's chairmen were not read, so no rulers are listed. The 1946-1957 Saar Protectorate is a separate state (saar-protectorate, eu-22-x) and is not covered here.
